title: On the shelf is not all free
hook: Six units are promised. Can every unit on the shelf serve a new request?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Separate physical inventory from uncommitted availability.

misconception: Every item physically present is available for a new request.
objective: Separate physical inventory from uncommitted availability.

claims.text: Six on-shelf units are already committed to earlier requests. Compare free and physical counts. Scaled model; six committed; no incoming stock.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At On-shelf=10, A=4items and B=10items. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-","x",6]]; B="x"; x denotes On-shelf. At x=10, A=4, B=10; recall at x=13: B=13. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Subtract committed units from the physical count to find free units. Commitments do not make the objects disappear, but they change which requests those objects can satisfy.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-","x",6]]; B="x"; x denotes On-shelf. At x=10, A=4, B=10; recall at x=13: B=13. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Six on-shelf units are already committed to earlier requests. Compare free and physical counts. Change only On-shelf to 13. What is B (Physical) now? Correct: 13items. Use B's stated rule with On-shelf=13: it gives 13items. Subtract committed units from the physical count to find free units. Commitments do not make the objects disappear, but they change which requests those objects can satisfy.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["max",0,["-","x",6]]; B="x"; x denotes On-shelf. At x=10, A=4, B=10; recall at x=13: B=13. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

recall.question: Six on-shelf units are already committed to earlier requests. Compare free and physical counts. Change only On-shelf to 13. What is B (Physical) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with On-shelf=13: it gives 13items. Subtract committed units from the physical count to find free units. Commitments do not make the objects disappear, but they change which requests those objects can satisfy.

safety.assumptions: Six on-shelf units are already committed to earlier requests. Compare free and physical counts.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
